column6: Launcher changes affect CLI dispatch and the installed command contract.
Path-security changes affect trusted-root, owner, mode, symlink, and deletion boundaries.
Quoting changes affect every rendered command and must preserve one-token argument boundaries.
Backup metadata policy changes affect format compatibility, restore selection, and property provenance.
Child cleanup changes affect signal-safe teardown and the process-start tokens that identify descendants.
CLI parsing changes are public interfaces and need golden-output coverage.
Dependency lookup changes affect secure PATH behavior and packaging.
Execution changes affect the single eval site for rendered commands, background shell isolation (setsid, shell job control or the cleanup wrapper), and process-group signalling.
Profiling changes affect operator-visible -V fields, timing counters, and measured helper-call budgets.
Module-order changes affect every launcher and direct-sourcing path.
Property-state changes affect the name-list zfs get parser (a security boundary), lone re-reads, serialization, cache invalidation, normalized lookup, and the recursive prefetch.
Property transfer changes affect -o parsing, readonly/-I/-U filtering, overrides, destination compatibility, and creation-time and inherited state.
SSH transport changes affect managed policy, wrapper argv, control sockets, and rendered/direct remote command channels.
Remote-host changes affect capability negotiation, remote helper resolution, and secure PATH propagation.
Replication orchestration changes affect planning, ordering, and convergence.
Reporting changes affect structured failures, operator-visible diagnostics, and the validated ZXFER_ERROR_LOG append.
Runtime changes affect temp-root selection, the private per-run temp root and its identity check, artifact allocation and readback, cleanup-PID tracking, and the run-root removal at exit.
Send/receive changes affect stream integrity and failure propagation.
Session ownership changes affect startup composition, remote connection preparation (control masters open before the first remote command), and teardown.

Snapshot-discovery changes affect source and destination listing commands, background producers, local and -T destination listings, failure diagnostics, normalization, diffing, the work lists, and the record files planning reads.
Migration-service changes affect platform-specific service stop/restart ordering and recovery after failure.
Send-job changes affect domain queue order, ancestry serialization, progress, and supervised completion.
Snapshot plan changes can alter GUID-aware planning, retention, deletion order, rollback eligibility, -g protection, divergence handling, and the live re-plan after -d deletes.
Destination-state changes affect existence checks and their cache, the destination dataset inventory, source-to-destination mapping, and the live depth-1 listing.
Unclassified source-module changes require launcher coverage and wider follow-up.
Budget-runner changes need caller-count, allow-list, list-output, and fail-closed fixture coverage.
Budget-policy changes need contract coverage and explicit ratchet justification.
Coverage-runner changes need report-contract tests.
Lint-runner changes must stay aligned with CI targets and lazy dependencies.
Man-page generator changes must preserve deterministic canonical-to-Solaris rendering.
Unit-runner changes need dispatch, ordering, and signal-cleanup coverage.
VM-runner changes need host-safe argument and guest-command tests.
Integration-harness changes need runner contracts before a manual guest run.
Performance-runner changes need artifact, argument-contract and --baseline-bin comparison tests.
Integration registry changes must preserve validated function names, pre-pool checks, filtering, and exact order.
CLI/reporting integration definitions affect usage errors, structured failures, diagnostics, and error-log behavior.
Snapshot/replication integration definitions affect retention, seeding, divergence, and convergence behavior.
Property/backup integration definitions affect reconciliation, metadata storage, and restore behavior.
Remote/security integration definitions affect secure PATH, SSH wrappers, capability protocols, and remote execution.
Jobs/platform integration definitions affect progress, supervision, cleanup, migration services, and platform behavior.
Hostile-input integration definitions affect dataset names with spaces and punctuation and property values with control characters, quotes and shell syntax, locally, with -j, and over -O/-T.
Future integration fragments must run the host-safe loader and safety-contract suite until they receive an explicit concern-specific mapping.
Integration fragment discovery (a sorted integration/*_tests.sh glob), the definition-only scan and registry parsing must stay non-eval and fail closed before pool access.
Shared unit lifecycle changes need runner cleanup coverage and a representative launcher suite.
Shared process-capture changes need runner supervision coverage and a representative launcher suite.
Shared loader changes affect full module loading and fragment registration.
Shared backup-fixture changes must run the stable backup-metadata suite entry point.
The exec fixture serves the exec entry and the fragments written for it in other homes.
The remote-host fixture serves the remote-host entry and the fragments written for it in other homes.
The runtime fixture serves the runtime entry and the session lifecycle fragment.
The send-job fixture serves the send-job entry and the exec background-shell fragment.
The property fixture serves the property state and property transfer entries.
The replication fixture serves the replication and migration-services entries, and its source-record staging the snapshot-plan live re-plan cases.
The snapshot-discovery fixture serves the discovery entry and the destination-state mapping fragment.
Environment-driven fake tools are sourced by the backup and reporting entries and by the exec, remote-host and snapshot-discovery fixtures.
Shared black-box helpers supply the lifecycle hooks and planning_* fixtures for every contract suite and the argv fuzz self-test.
Canned zfs, fixture, and runner changes affect every black-box and micro-bench consumer.
Micro-bench runner changes affect counted helper spawns, the advisory --forks rows, and the budget gate.
Micro-bench budget changes ratchet down only and need the headroom rule in the file header.
The minimal shared unit helper affects lifecycle, loading, capture, and explicit domain-fixture composition.
Shared ZFS fixture changes affect workdir boundaries, pool ownership, cleanup, and both direct harnesses.
Mock-remote fixture changes affect integration transport cases and remote performance scenarios.
The advisory A/B runner's argument contract, TSV and Markdown summary, harness errors, and baseline accommodations need runner tests.
The seeded argv fuzz drives the real launcher over hostile names and property values; runner changes need the fixed-seed and injected-fault self-tests.
The fuzz generator, model-backed fake zfs and checker must stay deterministic per seed and keep reporting split or changed arguments.
Validation-dispatch changes need safety-boundary and mapping tests.
Map changes need deterministic first-match selection tests.
Profile changes need closed-step dispatch tests.
The golden remote backup protocol scripts pin secure staging, publication order, rollback, quoting, and target-side command topology.
The golden remote capability probe pins secure PATH setup, helper discovery, optional-tool reporting, quoting, and status handling.
CLI golden files pin byte-exact help, usage-error, and failure-report output.
Changed unit suites should run themselves in the quick loop.
VM helper changes need host-side runner tests before guest execution.
Unclassified test-infrastructure changes need manual validation selection.
Workflow changes need local CI contract coverage.
GitHub metadata changes need workflow contract review.
Top-level guidance changes need documentation consistency review.
Contributor workflow changes need testing-guide consistency review.
Security guidance changes need trust-boundary documentation review.
Known-issue inventory changes need deduplication and evidence review.
Release-note changes need operator-facing accuracy review.
Documentation changes need link, spelling, and surface-consistency review.
Man-page changes must preserve the canonical section 8 page and reproducible Solaris rendering.
Example changes need CLI and safety consistency review.
Packaging changes need install-path and dependency review.
Agent-workflow changes need contributor-guidance review.
No focused mapping exists; run the full host-safe profile before merge.
